narrative.retroTreatment: A clearly framed late-eighties terminal window leads the hero: IBM Plex Mono headline and controls, a > prompt, and a low-contrast indigo grid on the existing ink-black canvas. The CV remains editorial. No extra accent colors, scanlines, or arcade ornament.
narrative.overview:
This is an engineer's workstation after hours: an ink-black canvas, one indigo signal, and a terminal window that makes the late-eighties reference immediately legible. The hero is framed like a compact console, with IBM Plex Mono, a > prompt, squared controls, and a low-contrast technical grid. The reference is clear but restrained: no arcade imagery, flashing effects, or added accent colors.

IBM Plex Mono carries the terminal headline, prompt, and hero controls. Newsreader remains in the brand mark and CV identity; Inter carries navigation, supporting copy, and the CV body. The first viewport gets a distinct workstation character while the long-form CV remains calm and readable.

Structurally the hero is a framed terminal window over a subtle indigo grid; the CV below remains a single editorial column with full-width hairlines. Color is nearly monochrome — zinc for nearly everything — with indigo reserved for the prompt, status signal, and actions. The grid and frame create the workstation silhouette without a second accent color or a full-site skin.
keyCharacteristics: Ink-black canvas with a one-color indigo signal.
A framed terminal hero, technical grid, monospace headline, and > prompt.
Newsreader for the brand/CV identity; Inter for navigation and reading copy.
CV remains flat and document-like, with full-width hairlines.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Indigo is the only chromatic color in the system and should occupy no more than ~10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point — if indigo is everywhere, nothing is signaled.

rules.name: The Selection Rule
rules.body: Text selection is the one other place indigo is allowed to appear: a 30%-opacity Signal Indigo wash (selection:bg-indigo-500/30). It never becomes a background fill.

rules.name: The Serif-For-Voice Rule
rules.body: Newsreader carries the brand and CV identity, plus italic prose. Inter handles navigation, supporting copy, and CV reading copy. IBM Plex Mono leads the hero headline, prompt, and controls. Never set navigation in the serif.

rules.name: The Terminal-For-Hero Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono leads the framed hero: headline, prompt, and actions. Keep supporting copy and CV prose readable in Inter.

rules.name: The Terminal Frame Rule
rules.body: The hero alone uses a bordered terminal window; the CV remains unboxed and document-like.

dos: Do use indigo as the only chromatic signal, including the hero grid and prompt.
Do use IBM Plex Mono for the hero headline, prompt, and hero controls; keep the CV body in Inter.
Do separate content with full-width Hairline borders rather than cards, boxes, or resting shadows.
Do apply the shared focus ring everywhere interactive: outline: 2px solid #818cf8; outline-offset: 2px.
Do keep the hero frame and controls squared; retain 8px compact CV actions.
donts: Don't introduce a second chromatic color, scanlines, or arcade decoration.
Don't frame or card the CV; the terminal window is a hero-only treatment.
Don't run supporting copy or CV prose in IBM Plex Mono.
